flagged.location: Remark — “Proper ideals and the empty case”
flagged.evidence: The remark says “the ideal I of interest later is proper and nonzero,” but the later associated-variety proposition allows any finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra and any two-sided ideal. Take g=0, so U(g)=C; the simple C-module C has annihilator I=0, which is primitive and proper but not nonzero. No restriction excluding this case is stated.
